newsitem.title: CHINA: Weak debut drags Shenzhen B index sharply down.
newsitem.headline: Weak debut drags Shenzhen B index sharply down.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended with sharp losses on Tuesday, badly hurt by a poor debut from Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, which became the year's first stock to close its first day with losses, analysts said.
The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index plunged 6.38 points or 5.00 percent to 121.30 points as turnover grew to HK$287.9 million from Monday's HK$50 million.

The domestic currency A share index rose 3.92 points or 1.04 percent to 382.27 on a short-term rebound after hitting an intraday low of 361.32. Turnover in the A share market was 5.3 billion yuan against Monday's 4.8 billion.
"Bengang fell below the offer price because no one wanted to buy shares in China's lumbering steel sector," said Peter Ho, an analyst at PBI Securities.
"The fact that a share ended its debut at a loss indicates a very bearish mood," Ho said.
The steel issue ended at HK$2.35, against the offer price of HK$2.38, after falling to a low of HK$1.90. Turnover in the stock reached HK$234 million.
"The share rebounded late in the afternoon as its relatively low P/E generated bargain-hunting," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
The B share market's P/E averaged about 15 times by Tuesday's close.

The steel company in June completed an initial public offering of 400 million B shares, carrying an earnings multiple of 8.0 times based on fully diluted 1996 per-share net profit of 0.318 yuan under international accounting standards.
Many of China's state-controlled steel companies, saddled with debt and burdened with bloated workforces, are unable to compete in the marketplace.
Analysts said they expected the A and B indices to fall further.
Market confidence waned after Hong Kong's transition to Beijing rule failed to lift indices as expected, analysts said.
"Our clients are nervous about further government clampdown measures," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Shenzhen's A and B shares have been hit by a long string of rumoured and actual government anti-speculation measures.
Bengang's performance pulled other new shares down, with Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd shedding HK$0.37 to HK$6.42 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
China Great Wall Computer Shenzhen was the best A share performer, ending 10 percent limit-up at 24.88 yuan.
